Done. Only `owns_paths` files touched.

**Changed:**
- `bridge/acp-pending.mjs` — new: `waitForPendingReply(history, chatId, {timeoutMs, pollMs})` polls history until the last assistant message after the last user message exists and is not `streaming`; returns its text or `""` on timeout.
- `bin/muse-acp.mjs` — `streamPendingReply` now waits via `waitForPendingReply` (`MUSE_PENDING_WAIT_MS`, default 30 s, 500 ms poll) instead of a single history read, so a reply Muse is still writing after an interrupt is delivered at the start of the next turn; fake driver got `MUSE_BRIDGE_FAKE_REPLY_LAG_MS` — a cancelled send lands its reply asynchronously (streaming partial at half-lag, full reply at lag), keeping the chat/message model identical.
- `tests/acp-pending.test.mjs` — unit: waits through missing → streaming → final `ALPHA`, `""` on timeout; integration: `MUSE_BRIDGE_FAKE_REPLY_LAG_MS=800` + cancel mid-reply, turn two's chunks are `PONG\n\nPONG` in the same chat.
- `bridge/session.mjs`, `tests/acp-cancel.test.mjs` — unchanged (all still pass).

APPROACH: Moved the pending-reply read into `bridge/acp-pending.mjs` as a poll loop keyed on "last user → last assistant, not streaming"; the fake now defers the reply past the cancel point under `MUSE_BRIDGE_FAKE_REPLY_LAG_MS`, so the integration test exercises the real wait path (missing → streaming → done) rather than an instant history hit.
LESSON: Recovery must poll for completion, not read once — a single history snapshot taken while Muse is still streaming silently drops the interrupted reply.

dispatchContext.rulesText:
- In verification scripts and tests that create temp dirs, use /tmp explicitly (mktemp -d /tmp/x.XXXXXX, or TMPDIR=/tmp): the writer sandbox denies mkdtemp in the system TMPDIR under /var/folders. Keep PM-written check scripts in /tmp/<name>/ (the guard blocks .mjs under .agents/).
- In a folder without git (live-folder mode), never put a task's expected_outputs or owns_paths under .bb/ (chat folders): the live snapshot skips .bb, so a file written there is never counted as produced and the task blocks as missing expected_outputs. Put task deliverables in a project folder such as docs/ or reports/.

Currently, 'bin/muse-acp.mjs' defines a naive inline 'promptText(prompt)' function that simply joins block text together without removing XML-like tags such as '<system_instructions>' or '<system-reminder>', violating the invariant that only user prompt text reaches Muse. Furthermore, 'bin/muse-acp.mjs' tracks sessions in memory and writes '{ accountId, museChatId }' to 'sessions.json' only after 'driver.send' resolves successfully. If a prompt turn is cancelled mid-flight, 'session.museChatId' is not updated or saved, leading to chat divergence on subsequent prompts.
